what_was_done: Added sole-cause rows to REFUSED_CALLS, one for each recorded revert: 'vsdd survey $x' and 'vsdd survey a$b' (a dollar sign is no safe character), 'vsdd survey a(b' (an opening parenthesis is no safe character; refused by the regular expression alone, since the parser refuses the text too), 'vsdd survey =a' written as "vsdd survey ='a'" (dropping the look-ahead that stops a quoted prefix from starting with '='), 'vsdd survey<CR>x' and 'vsdd survey<LF>x' (a carriage return or a line feed is no separator), '<CR>vsdd survey' (a carriage return is no leading blank), and 'sub=/vsdd survey', '=/vsdd survey', '=x/vsdd survey' (the program path holds no '=' in any position). Both table tests — through is_vsdd_call and the regular expression alone — hold every row, so each revert now fails a test whichever gate a future change loosens. Confirmation: in a scratch copy of next/, applied 137 mutations of the grammar — the recorded widenings (each of the 21 excluded characters and the single quote in the program's first and rest classes, '=' in the first class, '$' and '(' into _SAFE, the dropped prefix look-aheads, CR and LF into the separator and the leading blanks, and the per-code-point loosenings of the quoted-span class) plus quantifier and narrowing changes — and every one fails at least one of the pinning tests in test_caller.py, with the differential test a catcher in all 137 cases. The scratch caller.py was restored byte-identical after each run; the repository's caller.py was never modified.
